title: 860 Purchase Order Change Request — Business Data Object
description: The value an 860 Advanced Mapping JSONata expression must return. The expression's result REPLACES the native BDO (exposed as $defaultValues), so it must carry this whole shape — build on $defaultValues with the transform operator rather than constructing it from scratch. Every NetSuite-side identity (item, sales order, line) is resolved by the connector from the fields below; the BDO cannot name NetSuite records directly. See examples/860.md.

errors.description: Mapper errors. Carried into the reduce step but not consumed by the 860 processor; keep $defaultValues.errors.

yyyymmdd.description: X12 date as YYYYMMDD. Parsed with parseDate(yyyyMMdd) at apply time; an unparseable value fails the header change. null = no change requested for that date.

transactionId.description: ST02 transaction set control number. Informational only — never read by the applier.

purchaseOrderNumber.description: BCH03. Must equal (exact string match) the PO number of exactly one inbound 850 Orderful Transaction record; that 850's linked Sales Orders are the change targets. Zero or several matching 850s is a fatal error.

orderDate.description: BCH05 → custbody_orderful_edi_po_date on every targeted Sales Order (and trandate when the customer's Use 850 Date setting is on). Subject to the Allow Date Changes setting.

requestedShipDate.description: DTM*010 → shipdate. Subject to the Allow Date Changes setting.

startDate.description: DTM*196 → startdate. Subject to the Allow Date Changes setting.

endDate.description: DTM*197 → enddate. Subject to the Allow Date Changes setting.

earliestDelivery.description: DTM*064 → custbody_orderful_earliest_delivery. Subject to the Allow Date Changes setting.

latestDelivery.description: DTM*063 → custbody_orderful_latest_delivery. Subject to the Allow Date Changes setting.

hasStoreDistributions.description: True when any POC loop carried an SDQ segment. Informational only — the applier looks at each line's storeDistributions instead.

transactionLines.description: One entry per POC loop. Order does not matter; lines are matched to Sales Order lines by resolved NetSuite item, never by position or POC01.

userDefinedFields.description: Body-level custom fields (custbody_*) applied to EVERY Sales Order this 860 modifies, via setValue — or setText for ids listed in _textFields. 'T'/'F'/'true'/'false' strings are coerced to booleans; null/undefined values are skipped (the field is left unchanged).

_textFields.description: Field ids within userDefinedFields to apply with setText instead of setValue (dates, percentages, selects by display name). Note: on the 860 this sits beside userDefinedFields, not inside it.

changeCode.description: POC02 Change or Response Type Code. Decides which change(s) the line produces — see the change-code table in examples/860.md. Any other value fails the line.

quantity.description: POC03 Quantity Ordered. Carried, never applied.

quantity1.description: POC04 Quantity Left to Receive. THE new line quantity for quantity changes and additions — unless the line has storeDistributions, whose per-store quantity takes precedence. Must be a number, not a string.

unitPrice.description: POC08 unit price. New rate for price changes and additions; parsed with parseFloat. A price change with no unitPrice fails the line.

storeDistributions.description: From the POC loop's SDQ segments. When present, each entry targets ONE Sales Order (resolved from storeId) and supplies that order's quantity. Required for quantity changes on a PO split across several Sales Orders.

transactionLineId.description: Ignored. Present for historical reasons; the native mapper always emits null and the applier only interpolates it into error messages.

item.description: Product identifiers from the POC loop, bucketed by X12 235 qualifier. This is the ONLY input to item resolution: (1) an Orderful Item Lookup record with the matching qualifier code + exact value, else (2) the item master's SKU field (seller.vendorNumber || seller.vendorPartNumber) or UPC field (universal.upc || upcEANContainerCode || ean || eanUCC8). All three sub-objects must be present (null members are fine); a missing sub-object throws. Any other key — including netsuiteItemId — is ignored.

vendorNumber.description: VN — also matched against the item master SKU field

vendorPartNumber.description: VP — also matched against the item master SKU field

ean.description: EN — also matched against the item master UPC field

eanUCC8.description: EO — also matched against the item master UPC field

upc.description: UP — also matched against the item master UPC field

upcEANContainerCode.description: UK — also matched against the item master UPC field

storeId.description: SDQ identification code (store or DC number). Resolved to a Sales Order by: shipping-address store number, then DC number (DC-consolidated orders), then a line item's store number. No match fails the whole line.

storeIdQualifier.description: SDQ02 identification code qualifier (e.g. 92). Carried, never read.

quantity.description: Quantity for this store. Takes precedence over the line's quantity1 for the Sales Order this entry targets.

unitOfMeasure.description: SDQ01 unit. Carried, never read — the applied unit comes from the resolved item's sale unit.

type.description: Routes the transaction to the 860 processor after mapping. If this is missing or changed, processing fails with 'Unsupported transaction type'. Note the key is `metadata` on the 860 (the 850 BDO uses `metaData`).

metadata.description: Orderful transaction metadata as built by the native mapper. Keep $defaultValues.metadata as-is; only `type` is read downstream.
